name: Equip
one_liner: Virtual eating disorder treatment with a therapist, dietitian, medical provider and peer mentor; all 50 states, mostly paid by insurance.
best_for: Children and teens with anorexia, bulimia or ARFID whose families can take part in treatment at home
Adults with an eating disorder who want a specialist team without travelling to a clinic
People with private insurance or a participating Medicaid plan
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
People who are medically unstable and need hospital or residential care
People who rely on Medicare, which Equip does not accept
short_description: Equip treats eating disorders at home by video, using family-based treatment and CBT with a team of therapist, dietitian, medical provider and peer mentor.
long_description: Equip is a virtual eating disorder treatment program available in all 50 states. Each patient gets a care team made up of a therapist, a dietitian and a medical provider who specialise in eating disorders, plus a mentor with lived experience, and families take part in treatment. Care also includes support groups, skills workshops, real-time meal support and the Equip app. It treats anorexia, bulimia, binge eating disorder and ARFID. Equip is in network with most private insurers, including UnitedHealthcare, Aetna, Cigna, Blue Cross Blue Shield and Anthem, and some Medicaid plans; it does not take Medicare. Self-pay patients get a cost estimate before starting, with HSA/FSA and interest-free payment plans. Equip's own researchers have published a randomized comparison of two dietary approaches within its family-based treatment (100 patients) and an uncontrolled study of 783 patients treated for ARFID, in which weight and symptoms improved.

privacy.notes: Equip's medical practices follow a HIPAA notice for treatment records, but the website privacy policy says it shares personal information with third parties for targeted advertising when you browse without logging in.

seo.meta_description: Equip provides virtual eating disorder treatment for all ages with a family-based approach, including therapy, medical monitoring, and nutrition counseling.

faqs.a: FBT is the most effective evidence-based treatment for adolescent eating disorders. Parents/caregivers take an active role in helping their child recover, with therapist guidance. Equip adapts FBT principles for all ages, involving support people in treatment.

faqs.q: What's included in the Equip treatment team?
faqs.a: Each patient gets a 5-person team: therapist for individual/family therapy, dietitian for nutrition rehabilitation, physician for medical monitoring, peer mentor (someone in recovery), and family mentor (a parent who supported recovery). They coordinate your comprehensive care.

Yes, Equip accepts most major insurance plans for eating disorder treatment. Coverage varies by plan. Contact them to verify your specific benefits before starting. Insurance often covers telehealth eating disorder treatment at similar rates to in-person care.

faqs.q: Who are the peer and family mentors?
faqs.a: Peer mentors are people with lived eating disorder recovery experience. Family mentors are parents who've supported a loved one through recovery. They provide unique support and hope that comes from having 'been there'—complementing clinical treatment.

citation.journal: Eating Disorders: The Journal of Treatment & Prevention

clinical_trials.outcome: A daily calorie target and the Plate-by-Plate approach led to similar weight gain and eating disorder symptom improvement; caregivers rated the calorie target as more effective.
clinical_trials.study_design: Randomized comparative effectiveness study (two active arms, no untreated control); 76 analysed

clinical_trials.study: Naturalistic study of Equip's virtual ARFID treatment

citation.authors: Hellner M, Cai K, Freestone D, Baker JH, Menzel J, Steinberg DM
citation.title: Clinical Outcomes in a Large Sample of Youth and Adult Patients Receiving Virtual Evidence-Based Treatment for ARFID: A Naturalistic Study

clinical_trials.outcome: Youth and adults on weight restoration moved closer to target weight, and ARFID symptoms, anxiety and depression improved. No control group.

patient_summary: You and your family meet your Equip team by video: a therapist, a dietitian, a medical provider and a peer mentor, with meal support and groups in between. Most private insurance plans and some Medicaid plans cover it; you can check your plan with Equip's insurance screener or get a self-pay estimate before you start.
